done_when: The worker brief (both tools) explicitly invites the worker to spawn the repo's subagent roles when the work splits into independent parts (an explorer to trace code paths, a tester to write tests while it builds, separate files edited in parallel), at most 3 at a time, and to do small tasks itself; Codex workers' thread config keeps multi_agent on and uses forge.toml's subagent model and effort. New and existing repos: every repo gets it from the new release and its next forge sync; nothing in forge.toml changes. One command-level test: the brief sent to a Codex worker and a Claude worker carries the invitation, and the Codex thread config enables multi-agent.
why: Codex spawns subagents only when explicitly asked, and Forge's worker brief never asks, so no Forge worker ever delegates: the repo's subagent roles and the subagent models in forge.toml go unused
